Subject: Hosted API evaluation: deployment-mode eligibility & quickstart next steps

Hi Emily / Jake —

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier today. Quick recap and proposed next steps now that we have the basic scope:

What we heard
- Primary goal: integrate an in-product assistant and policy-driven prompt reranking for checkout support flows.
- Target traffic for evaluation: 500–1,200 queries/day initially, with occasional bursts up to ~50 qps for 10–15 minutes during promotions.
- Data concerns: CheckoutAI wants to keep PII out of logs and prefers US-only processing for the pilot.

Redwood recommendation for the pilot
- Start on Hosted API (fastest path) — low-friction API keys, no infra setup, immediate access to curated models and streaming.
- Hosted supports region selection (US-only) and can be configured to avoid persistent logging of fields you mark as sensitive.
- If you later need strict network isolation or on-prem data residency, we’d transition to Private. Dedicated is recommended when sustained peak qps > 200 for predictable throughput.

Quickstart steps I can own this week
1) Share a short quickstart checklist and sample rate-limit file (attached).
2) Provision a restricted API key scoped to your test endpoints.
3) Provide sample endpoint URL and token limits for the pilot traffic profile.

Questions for you
- Can you confirm expected concurrent users during the 50 qps bursts and whether those requests are short (<= 256 tokens) or long (>= 1k tokens)?
- Any procurement timing or PO requirements we should plan for?

Next steps
- I’ll attach the quickstart checklist and a sample CSV showing rate tiers. Ben (cc) will follow up with an SRE-friendly summary of rate limits and header suggestions for masking PII.
- If you’re good, let’s schedule a 30-min ops call tomorrow or Friday to provision the key and run a small smoke test.

Attachments: quickstart-checklist.pdf (stub), rate-limit-sample.csv (stub)

Thanks, Naomi — really helpful recap. A couple quick clarifications before we lock the ops call: 

On rate limits and burst handling
- The 50 qps bursts are mostly for cart-abandonment campaigns; they last ~10–15 minutes. Peak concurrent users would be ~45–60 during those windows. Most requests are short (~120 tokens).

On data residency and logging
- For the evaluation we can avoid sending PII, but procurement will ask whether logs (audit / request traces) can be disabled or stored only in US regions. Is that supported by Hosted?

On procurement
- We may need a short MSA addendum and a standard security questionnaire answered (we’ll send the questionnaire tomorrow). Also curious whether you recommend Hosted vs Dedicated if we expect to go to 5–10k qps within 12–18 months (longer-term planning).

If you can confirm the above, we’ll pick a time for the ops smoke test.

From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.ai>

Emily — thanks for the quick notes. Short answers and a few specifics you can hand to procurement / SRE: 

1) Burst and concurrency
- Hosted API supports short bursts via token buckets. For the 50 qps / ~60 concurrent users profile we recommend the "burst-cap" tier we discussed; default throttling is per API key (we can configure a burst window to match your promo length).

2) Token & payload limits
- Single request max payload: 4,096 tokens. For your ~120 token median requests you’ll be well within normal limits.
- Streaming is supported for longer LLM responses if you plan to surface assistant typing.

3) Logging / data residency
- Hosted: you can opt out of request/response persistence for specific API keys; audit logs (control-plane events) remain for account security but can be restricted to US regions. We’ll provide the required SOC2-backed evidence.

4) Long-term scale guidance
- If you expect sustained peaks approaching thousands of qps (5–10k) within a year, Dedicated becomes the predictable option (reserved GPU pools). Private is typical for strict networking / on-prem needs. We can model a cost/latency projection for both.

Attachments: quickstart-checklist.pdf (stub), rate-limit-sample.csv (stub)
